newsitem.title: USA: ITT Hartford maps reinsurance growth.
newsitem.headline: ITT Hartford maps reinsurance growth.

text.p: With the global reinsurance market increasingly dominated by a few big players, ITT Hartford Group Inc intends to stay in the game by nurturing its own reinsurance growth.

"We need to look at the possibility of acquisition," John Donahue, The Hartford's senior vice president and chairman of its reinsurance operation, Hartford Re Company (HartRe), told Reuters in an interview.
"In 1997 we see continued geographic and product-line expansion."
The 186-year-old company is now the nation's 11th biggest reinsurer, with premium income expected to grow by 20-21 percent this year to $560 million, said Donahue.
"We're looking at 25 percent growth in 1997 and again in 1998," he said.
Donahue said HartRe will rev up an aggressive game plan by opening several new offices next year, including one in Malaysia -- a promising market that recently opened its doors to foreign reinsurers.
The property and casualty reinsurer also hopes to open an office in Miami to handle Latin American business, as well as another office somewhere in the midwestern United States.
Donahue said HartRe's October acquisition of San Francisco Re's renewal rights, for an undisclosed price, was significant.
"We will use that business to expand up and down the West Coast and as a further expansion into the Far East."
HartRe also bought the renewal rights of Farmington, Conn.-based SecurityRe Companies, a unit of Orion Capital, on November 14.
Through both deals "All of a sudden, we're looking at renewal rights of $230-235 million that we didn't have in the early part of 1996," said Donahue.

The Hartford has been serious about revamping its reinsurance operation since 1992. But the move received fresh impetus after last year's spinoff from diversified ITT Corp and the ascension of Ramani Ayer as chairman-elect in September, said Donahue.
"We clearly see HartRe as a billion-dollar company before the end of the decade," said Donahue.
As a percentage of The Hartford's total business, HartRe should grow to seven percent by 2000 from five percent now.

Though HartRe is still dwarfed by industry giants such as Munich Re, Swiss Re and General Re, the recent spate of acquisitions within the industry actually presents HartRe with growth opportunities, said Donahue.
"The (reinsurance) giants will need (time to) digest these huge mergers and make them work. They will be very busy doing that. Underneath that, I think you'll still see mergers and acquisitions.

"Any company in the business that's writing less than $200 million probably is going to ask itself what's it's doing in the business of reinsurance. That is going to give an opportunity for HartRe to expand."
